static_traits.name: Li Jie
static_traits.family_status: Married to his wife; has a 10-year-old son
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive wife, but has not yet discussed specific worries about their son's soccer performance with her
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet experienced similar psychological problems, has not yet received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, able to be self-aware and to name cognitive patterns (such as overgeneralization and catastrophizing); restrained tone, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling disappointed and inadequate after her son missed a tackle in a football game, frequently catastrophizing and overgeneralizing his ability, affecting her mood and interaction with her son; the problem worsened after his wife's unemployment.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent negative thinking and disappointment are affecting my relationship with my son and overall well-being, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: Failure means never being good enough
Only sustained outstanding results count as success

special_situations.event: In the most recent game, the son missed a key tackle
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he makes a mistake in a game, it means he will never be good enough and is not suited for sports
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: More harsh toward the son, emphasizing results to reduce repeated mistakes; tries to rationally persuade themselves by emphasizing 'effort matters more than results' but finds it hard to change the mindset
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will never play soccer well

special_situations.event: During the son's training or competition, sees him show ordinary performance or make mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he cannot consistently perform well, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Highly tense while watching and fault-finding; criticizing and pressuring after the game
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: His performance is not good enough, which means he will not improve later either

special_situations.event: After his wife's unemployment, overall increased stress in the family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When the family is under stress, the son's poor performance will trigger worse consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing anxiety on controlling and criticizing the son's performance to gain certainty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Once he performs poorly now, the future will only get worse

special_situations.event: Thinking about whether to share with his wife his worries about their son's performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should solve problems myself; expressing to my wife will make her more worried
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing not to discuss specific worries with his wife to avoid 'adding to her burden'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not trouble her with this

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a responsible, supportive good parent whose child excels in sports
core_conflict.fear: Fearing the child will fail, fearing being an incompetent parent
defense_goal: Relieving anxiety and maintaining a sense of control by criticizing and controlling the child's performance
Avoids expressing worries to his wife to avoid increasing her stress

object_relations.self_representation: An anxious and harsh parent, worried about the child failing
object_relations.object_representation: A child who needs correcting, not good enough (not suited for sports)

object_relations.self_representation: A partner who should bear pressure alone
object_relations.object_representation: A partner who needs protection and is already under pressure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks whether one would discuss specific worries with one's wife or suggests sharing with one's wife
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes sharing will increase his wife's burden and that he should bear it alone (transference: seeing his partner as a fragile person who needs protection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle, restrained tone emphasizing 'I do not want her to worry more''I should handle it myself', reducing emotional expression and avoiding in-depth discussion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the son makes a mistake or performs ordinarily in a game
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Transforming anxiety about family and financial pressure into criticism and control of the son's performance (transference: attributing external pressure to the child's performance)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaking faster, in a tense tone, using absolutist words (e.g. 'always''must') to make harsh comments or suggestions.

manifestations: Unwilling to share specific worries with his wife, feeling he should bear them alone
Choosing to cope alone when family stress is high
outcomes: Increased emotional burden with the support system not yet fully utilized
Weakened emotional connection with partner, increased subjective sense of isolation

manifestations: Takes 'I should handle it myself' as an inner rule and takes on excessive responsibility
outcomes: Ability to seek help in relationships is limited, contact with resources decreases

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly emphasizes 'I should be able to handle it myself', restraining expression for fear of burdening his wife
Restrained tone in counseling, carefully stating own worries

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking support from his wife, pressing stress onto himself
Internalizing anxiety into harshness and control toward himself and parent-child interactions

positive_force: Has a supportive wife and family resources
Willing to change with a positive attitude; can cooperate with counseling and homework
Has awareness of her cognitive biases (able to identify catastrophizing and overgeneralization)
Willing to try reframing perspectives and behavioral experiments
negative_force: Strong cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and black-and-white thinking
Mental filtering, over-focusing on the son's mistakes
Under stress, reduces communication with the partner, forming subjective isolation
Increased family stress from his wife's unemployment
Being overly harsh with the son, parent-child relationship damaged

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking about the son's games or training, with excessive harshness toward him
antecedent: Watching the son's soccer games or training
The son makes a mistake (e.g. missing a tackle)
Overall rising stress after his wife's unemployment
target_behavior.core_reason: Against a background of rising family stress, equating a single mistake with permanent failure through overgeneralization, failure prediction, and black-and-white thinking, seeking certainty through control and criticism
target_behavior.function: Reducing anxiety through criticism and control, avoiding perceived potential failure and gaining a subjective sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child relationship tension; reduced work focus; impaired mood and self-care
